definitions.explanation: Bite-sized pieces of meat (usually chicken) marinated, coated with flour or starch, and deep-fried.

examples.japanese: {鶏|とり}の{唐揚|からあ}げを{作|つく}りました。
{唐揚|からあ}げにレモンを{絞|しぼ}る。
examples.english: Squeeze lemon on the fried chicken.
examples.notes: A common but sometimes controversial practice

examples.japanese: {居酒屋|いざかや}の{定番|ていばん}メニューは{唐揚|からあ}げだ。
examples.english: Fried chicken is a standard izakaya menu item.

examples.japanese: お{弁当|べんとう}に{唐揚|からあ}げを{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I put fried chicken in the bento.

examples.japanese: {揚|あ}げたての{唐揚|からあ}げにレモンをかけるかどうかで{友達|ともだち}と{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれた。
examples.english: My friends and I disagreed over whether to squeeze lemon on freshly fried karaage.

notes:
Also written as {空揚|からあ}げ or から{揚|あ}げ. The {唐|から} refers to China/foreign style, though the dish is distinctly Japanese.

Preparation typically involves:
1. Marinating in {醤油|しょうゆ}, {酒|さけ}, {生姜|しょうが}, にんにく
2. Coating with {片栗粉|かたくりこ} or {小麦粉|こむぎこ}
3. Deep-frying until golden and crispy

{大分|おおいた}{県|けん}{中津|なかつ}{市|し} is famous as a karaage town. The debate over whether to squeeze lemon on shared karaage ({レモン{論争|ろんそう}}) is a common topic.

Similar: {竜田揚|たつたあ}げ (uses potato starch only, often with soy sauce marinade).
